background.fact: Microsoft controls the BMP raster image family, used originally on Windows and OS/2.
BMP version 5 arrived with Windows 98 in 1998.
BMP commonly stores uncompressed pixels, although lossless compression is available.
Version 5 can record an ICC profile and an alpha channel.
BMP is commonly encountered in Windows screen captures and system graphics.
The registered BMP media type is image/bmp.

windows.note: Lists BMP among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

mac.note: Lists BMP among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

linux.note: Lists BMP among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

web.note: Displays BMP pictures in browser content.
Supports BMP images according to Mozilla’s browser compatibility table.

problems.fact: An uncompressed BMP can be bulky; PNG or JPEG may be more practical for distribution.
A program expecting an older bitmap header may need BMP3 or BMP2 output rather than the default BMP version.
A BMP does not preserve editable vector shapes or live typography.

background.fact: ICO is Microsoft's image format for graphical interface icons.
The file may contain more than one image.
ICO files use little-endian byte ordering.
The registered media type is image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
The .ico extension is widely associated with website favicons.
Windows Vista icon guidance includes 256-by-256 images for high-DPI displays.

windows.note: Lists ICO among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

mac.note: Lists ICO among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

linux.note: Lists ICO among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

web.note: Displays ICO pictures in browser content.
Supports ICO images according to Mozilla’s browser compatibility table.

problems.fact: Malformed image offsets can confuse an ICO reader; an invalid header is different from a missing file association.
A small icon enlarged for a high-DPI display may look soft; include a suitable larger image in the icon.
An ICO may contain multiple images, so check its variants instead of assuming the first preview is the only image.

background.fact: A .wmv file uses the ASF container with Windows Media coded content.
ASF was designed for synchronized media storage and network delivery.
The container can accommodate audio and video streams.
ASF supports delivery from a local disk or an HTTP server.
WMV files can use Windows Media Video 7, 8, or 9 compression.
The Library of Congress records video/x-ms-wmv as a commonly used media type, rather than an IANA registration.

windows.note: Lists ASF/WMV input and Windows Media Video 1, 2, and 9 decoding.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play WMV input.

mac.note: Lists ASF/WMV input and Windows Media Video 1, 2, and 9 decoding.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play WMV input.

linux.note: Lists ASF/WMV input and Windows Media Video 1, 2, and 9 decoding.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play WMV input.

mobile.note: The Android port includes the desktop player's media decoding features.
Plays local media using VLC's player rather than requiring conversion through the system player.

problems.fact: A player's decoder coverage matters: FFmpeg lists its Windows Media Video 9 decoder as not completely working.
Image fidelity depends on the codec and compression settings, so the WMV ending alone does not establish quality.
Reading ASF and decoding its video are separate capabilities; a compatible container reader does not guarantee every codec is present.

background.fact: FLAC compresses integer PCM audio without discarding sample information.
Its specification is open, and its reference implementation is open source.
RFC 9639 standardized the format description in December 2024.
The format supports one through eight channels and sample depths from four through 32 bits.
A native FLAC stream uses the audio/flac media type.
FLAC metadata can include seek points, pictures, and Vorbis comments.

windows.note: Imports FLAC directly without the optional FFmpeg library.
Lists FLAC as an input format and a decoded audio codec.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play FLAC input.

mac.note: Imports FLAC directly without the optional FFmpeg library.
Lists FLAC as an input format and a decoded audio codec.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play FLAC input.

linux.note: Imports FLAC directly without the optional FFmpeg library.
Lists FLAC as an input format and a decoded audio codec.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play FLAC input.

web.note: Decodes FLAC audio; the documented native container is supported.
FLAC decoding is listed in Mozilla’s browser support comparison.

mobile.note: The Android port includes the desktop player's media decoding features.
Plays local media using VLC's player rather than requiring conversion through the system player.

problems.fact: A damaged frame can fail its checksum; lossless encoding does not prevent storage corruption.
Changing a lossy source to FLAC cannot recreate the audio samples that were removed earlier.
Android's documented native FLAC support is narrower than the format: mono or stereo audio, with 16-bit samples recommended.

background.fact: The WebM Project promotes an open media format intended for web delivery.
The container is based on Matroska.
WebM combines VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis or Opus audio.
The project supplies its format technology under royalty-free terms.
WebM video uses video/webm; an audio-only WebM uses audio/webm.

windows.note: Reads Matroska-family media; codec support must match the WebM streams.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play WEBM input.

mac.note: Reads Matroska-family media; codec support must match the WebM streams.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play WEBM input.

linux.note: Reads Matroska-family media; codec support must match the WebM streams.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play WEBM input.

web.note: Safari 14.1 added WebM files with VP8/VP9 video and Vorbis sound.

mobile.note: The Android port includes the desktop player's media decoding features.
Plays local media using VLC's player rather than requiring conversion through the system player.

problems.fact: Browser playback depends on the actual video and audio codecs, rather than the WebM suffix alone.
A missing cue index can make seeking less efficient because the player has less direct location information.
Older Safari behavior should not be generalized to current releases: Safari 14.1 added macOS playback for WebM with VP8 or VP9 and Vorbis.

background.fact: MPEG-2 was developed for compressed television delivery and later adopted for DVDs.
MPEG systems organize coded picture, sound, and data as streams.
An elementary stream represents one coded media component.
Packetized elementary streams divide those components into packets.
The .mpeg and .mpg suffixes are both used for MPEG video files.
The Library of Congress records video/mpeg for MPEG video.

windows.note: Lists MPEG elementary, program, and transport streams as readable input.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play MPEG input.

mac.note: Lists MPEG elementary, program, and transport streams as readable input.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play MPEG input.

linux.note: Lists MPEG elementary, program, and transport streams as readable input.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play MPEG input.

mobile.note: The Android port includes the desktop player's media decoding features.
Plays local media using VLC's player rather than requiring conversion through the system player.

problems.fact: An MPEG file may be a system stream or raw video; identifying its structure helps choose the correct demuxer.
A player must decode the audio as well as the video; multiplexing them does not make their codecs interchangeable.
Lossy MPEG encoding cannot retain every detail from the uncompressed picture.

background.fact: PSD is Adobe Photoshop's native document file format.
The PSD header begins with the signature 8BPS.
PSD dimensions are limited to 30,000 pixels per side; PSB raises that limit.
The header supports sample depths of one, eight, 16, or 32 bits.
Image resources and layer/mask information occupy separate sections.
Pixel data can be raw or encoded with RLE or ZIP compression.
The registered PSD media type is image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.

windows.note: Lists PSD among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

mac.note: Lists PSD among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

linux.note: Lists PSD among supported image formats; company use requires a license.

web.note: Uses PSD as its main document format and opens files through File > Open.

problems.fact: A document larger than the PSD dimension limit needs PSB or another suitable format.
A PSD includes layer and mask information that a simple flattened image export does not retain.
Third-party readers must interpret Photoshop-specific data structures; opening a preview does not establish full editing compatibility.

background.fact: FLV is a binary format associated with Macromedia Flash video delivery.
An FLV holds at most one video stream and one audio stream.
FLV can carry Sorenson video or On2 VP6 video.
Audio possibilities include MP3, PCM, and ADPCM.
A Flash SWF can reference a separate FLV through ActionScript.
Adobe ended Flash Player support on December 31, 2020.

windows.note: Lists FLV input plus Sorenson and VP6-family decoding.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play FLV input.

mac.note: Lists FLV input plus Sorenson and VP6-family decoding.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play FLV input.

linux.note: Lists FLV input plus Sorenson and VP6-family decoding.
Uses FFmpeg decoders to play FLV input.

mobile.note: The Android port includes the desktop player's media decoding features.
Plays local media using VLC's player rather than requiring conversion through the system player.

problems.fact: Flash Player is discontinued, so reinstalling it is not an appropriate route to playing an old FLV.
The FLV extension does not identify a unique video codec; a reader also needs the stream's decoder.
A workflow requiring multiple alternative audio tracks cannot retain that structure inside the one-audio-stream FLV model.
